articleTitle: The transfinite element method for computing electromagnetic scattering from arbitrary lossy cylinders
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A new numerical procedure called the transfinite element method is used to solve two-dimensional electromagnetic scattering problems involving lossy dielectric cylinders. In this procedure, the problem region is divided into two parts: A circular region<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{i}</tex>of finite extent that must enclose all scatterers and an exterior region<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{e}</tex>surrounding<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{j}</tex>that is homogeneous and unbounded. Within<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{i}</tex>finite element basis functions are used to approximate the electromagnetic field; in<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R_{e}</tex>the separation of variables technique is used to find a complete set of basis functions for the field. Requiring continuity along the circular boundary in a variational procedure then provides a matrix equation that is solved to compute the scattered field.

articleTitle: Low-cost microstrip phased array antenna for use in mobile satellite telephone communication service
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A design for a low-cost phased array antenna used in a car-top application for a satellite communications link is presented. Microstrip stacked patch elements provide good pattern coverage over the 7% bandwidth. Three-bit distributed element microstrip phase shifters provide beam steering over a range of 30 to 70 degrees from boresight. Microstrip technology is also used in the corporate power divider and polarization hybrids. A hybrid tracking system consisting of an inertial sensor for open loop tracking and a sequential lobing scheme for closed loop tracking provides accurate tracking of the signal through brief signal outages. A novel scheme is used to eliminate the effects of varying multipath on closed-loop tracking accuracy. A single board PC-compatible computer is used in conjunction with an interface board to steer the antenna and interface with the transceiver.

abstract: We are developing an innovative microwave-integrated-circuits class at Caltech that uses personal computers to design and analyze microstrip circuits, and to make the artwork and measurements. We have written an interactive microwave computer-aided-design program, Puff, that is quite fast at laying out and analyzing microstrip circuits. articleTitle: Theoretical near field clutter and interference cancellation for an adaptive phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Displaced phase center antennas with adaptive nulling capability are sometimes suggested for airborne radar applications requiring cancellation of clutter and interference. A theoretical model is developed for analyzing a linear array having two independent beamformers, which is subjected to near-field or far-field clutter and interference. Both clutter and interference are modeled using discrete noise sources. It is demonstrated that an adaptive array cancels such near field and far field sources in a nearly equivalent manner.

articleTitle: "Compact ranges - Past, present, and future"
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: The compact range has been used for electromagnetic measurements since the early 1950's. Although the early attempts with such systems had some successes, they were not generally used until the middle of the 1970's. This recent interest was sparked by a commercially available system developed by Scientific-Atlanta. This system was specifically designed and tested for antenna applications, even though the earlier tests were made in terms of scattering measurements. Based on the recent interest in radar cross-section, the compact range has been re-examined in terms of its capabilities for measuring the scattering properties of large structures. The Ohio State University has been one of the pioneers in developing the proper use. capabilities; and modifications necessary to make the compact range one of the most accurate electromagnetic pattern measurement systems available. As a result, new systems have been designed using various electromagnetic analyses to guide this research effort. These changes include the reflector, feeds, target mount, instrumentation, absorber, target handling techniques, data processing, calibration methods, calibration targets, etc. In most cases, the theoretical solutions have been verified by experimental results, and in some cases, the new designs have been incorporated in Commericial products. The presentation will attempt to cover the latest and more interesting aspects of this challenging new area.

articleTitle: An exact mutual coupling theory for microstrip patches
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An accurate determination of mutual coupling between microstrip antennas is important in the design of finite arrays of patch elements. The classical formula for mutual impedance based on reciprocity is popular for determining such coupling. However, this formula ignores the presence of other open-circuited elements and consequently has serious limitations in accuracy due to resonant currents which may exist on such elements. In this presentation an exact theory for the mutual coupling between eatch elements will be presented, which circumvents this difficulty. For very weak coupling the exact formula reduces to the classical formula.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-wave antennas an thin membranes
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Submillimeter-wave antennas with bismuth microbolometer detectors have been fabricated on 1-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">\mu</tex>m thick silicon-oxynitride membranes. This approach results in better patterns than previous lens-coupled integrated circuit antennas, and eliminates the dielectric loss associated with the substrate lens. Measurements on a wideband log-periodic antenna at 700 GHz, 380 GHz and 167 GHz, and on a 700 GHz log-periodic imaging array, show no sidelobee and a 3-dB beamwidth between<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40\deg</tex>and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50\deg</tex>. Also, the effective area can be increased by 5 dB by the use of a back-shorting mirror. Possible application areas are superconducting tunnel junction receivers for radio astronomy and imaging arrays for plasma diagnostics.

articleTitle: Analysis of frequency behavior of slot arrays
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: While slot arrays are usually designed at midband frequency, it is often useful to evaluate the input match bandwidth, beam deflection, and pattern distortion occuring when frequency changes. A perturbation method is presented here for analysing the frequency behavior of arrays of longitudinal slots fed by an air-filled or dielectric-filled rectangular waveguide. The two examples discussed, a resonant array and a traveling wave array show good agreement between experimental and theoretical results, and give an insight into the severe frequency limitations on slot arrays.

articleTitle: A method to analyze scattering from general periodic screens using fast fourier transform and conjugate gradient method
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A technique to analyze general periodic screens is presented. This technique uses the Conjugate Gradient (CG) method and the aliasing effects that appear when discretizing the Green's function in the spectral domain. The technique is computationally efficient because it does not require any summation of Floquet's harmonics in the real domain and because using the FFT to evaluate the convolutions that appear in the CG method reduces the computing time and avoids the manipulations of large matrices. Some results of current distributions are presented.

articleTitle: High-frequency beam wave propagation in a turbulent stratified ionosphere
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: High-frequency, (HF) beam wave propagation in a turbulent stratified ionosphere is investigated using the amplitude-phase-screen approach. At oblique incidence, the beam wave is refracted in the ionosphere with its amplitude and phase calculated by geometrical optics approximation. The diffraction from the bottom of the ionosphere down to the ground is taken into account by Fresnel formula. Numerical results are obtained under the assumption of the one-dimensional Gaussian correlated irregularities. It turns out that the coherence bandwidth of the wave is greatly reduced as the strength of random irregularities increases.

Comparing this technique with MM the computer time is reduced orders of magnitude and storage of large matrices is not required. Therefore problems of bodies of arbitrary geometry with sizes of several wavelengths can be handled rigurously. To check the method results of RCS of circular and square plates are presented and compared with analytical or measured results avalaible in the literature [1], [2], [3]. Excelent agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: Diode-grids for millimeter-wave phase-shifters and frequency doublers
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Diode-grids have been fabricated on 2-cm square monolithic gallium-arsenide wafers with 1600 Schottky varactor-diodes. A computer-controlled reflectometer that uses a wave-front division interference technique was developed to measure the reflection coefficient of the diode-grids. A<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">70\deg</tex>phase shift with a 6-dB loss was obtained at 93 GHz when the bias on the diode-grid was changed from -3V to +1V. A second harmonic conversion efficiency of 16 % and an output power of 0.5 W was obtained at 66 GHz when the diode-grid was pumped with a pulsed magnetron at 33 GHz.

abstract: By means of electrostatics and transmission line theory, the equivalent transmission line method has been complemented and corrected so that to be used to evaluate the input impedance of cylindrical doublet antennas. A more accurate calculation formula has been developed,in which the loss along the equivalent transmission line and the end-effects have been taken into account. Numerical and experimental results obtained show that this corrected formula is adaptable to thick cylindrical antennas and gives more accurate result with less mathematical complication than both Hallen's integral equation method and Schelkunoff's biconical antenna theory.

articleTitle: A new method of aperture analysis and synthesis via Gaussian beam expansion
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An arbitary function f(x), defined In the finite interval [-l,l], may be expressed in terms of a series of modulated Gaussian functions. This kind of series representation has several advantages. First of all unlike the ordinary Fourier series representation, it is no longer a periodic function. Secondly, FFT method can be applied to evaluate the expansion coefficients. Finally, intesrals connected to f(x) and mostly invloved in aperture analysis and synthesis problems can be performed in closed form. The numerical results show that this kind of function expansion is really promising in the aperture analysis and synthesis applications.

articleTitle: Application of Maxwell to undergraduate electromagnetics instruction
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: Maxwell is a comprehensive package of computer programs for modelling electromagnetic field problems by using the finite element method. It consists of an input module called Meshmaker for specifying the problem geometry and for creating the finite element mesh and a number of solution modules for solving for the propagation and radiation characteristics of transmission lines, waveguides, planar circuits, and antennas. It has been used with the IBM PC and the HP Bobcat in various forms in six undergraduate classes to aid in understanding fields.

articleTitle: Computer architecture implications of the numerical solution for the electromagnetic field of an arbitrary current source
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: An algorithm has been specified for the hardware implementation of the numerical solution of the electromagnetic fields of an arbitrary current source. The algorithm solves for the magnetic (H) and electric (E) fields, as well as the vector potential (A) of a finite length arbitrary current source. A mid-point summation technique was employed and tested by simulation. The simulation was accomplished with a single<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</tex>-directed dipole,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10 \lambda</tex>long, for the test antenna. Numerical solutions utilizing uniform and triangular envelope current distributions were compared with the far-field solution for the test antenna at ranges of 250 and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">500 \lambda</tex>. The number of sub-elements simulated in the mid-point summation were 50, 100, and 500. When 500 subelements were used the difference between the numerical and far-field solutions decreased to less than 1 percent for 95 percent of the observation points. The greatest differences between the numerical and far-field solutions occurred in the null regions of the radiation pattern. The algorithm is inherently symmetric with respect to the cartesian coordinate system and, as such, lends itself to highly parallel and concurrent computational techniques. This property of the algorithm makes it an excellent candidate for implementation by a Very High Speed Integrated Circuit (VHSIC) class processor. Investigation of a parallel, highly concurrent architectural implementation has yielded preliminary results that computational savings of 5 orders of magnitude is attainable.

articleTitle: Coaxial waveguide diplexing circuit using a corrugated waveguide transition
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: A technique using corrugated-wall waveguide to separate the energy from two frequency bands into concentric coaxially disposed circular waveguides is discussed. The corrugation depth is chosen so that the reactance sign of the surface impedance changes between the two frequency bands. This has the effect of matching the respective field distributions fo the coaxially disposed waveguides. A unique low-pass filter added fo the coaxial waveguide supports the center conductor and further enhances the isolation between the two frequency bands.

articleTitle: A new course on computer methods in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: With the prolification of computers in university campuses, there is a significant need to introduce more courses on "computer methods" in the engineering curriculum. This paper summarizes our two-year experience with a new "computer techniques in electromagnetics" course which we introduced as an elective for seniors. Main features of the new course include: 1) The inclusion of the Finite Difference method for solving engineering problems formulated in terms of partial differential equations as well as the Method of Moments for solving integral equations, 2) The Finite Element was also introduced and special emphasis were placed on derivation of the functionals to be minimized using this method, 3) The Finite Difference method was used to solve modern engineering problems such as the design of microstrip transmission lines and eigenvalue problems such as waveguides of arbitrary cross sections, and 4) The Method of Moment was used to solve static and dynamic field problems including radiation from linear antennas and scattering from two-dimensional inhomogeneous dielectric objects. Key steps in developing the course will be discussed and results from the various computer programs written by the students will be presented.

articleTitle: Radar cross-section of a flat plate with two face impedance
publicationTitle: 1987 Antennas and Propagation Society International Symposium
abstract: This paper examines the problem of electromagnetic scattering of a flat plate whose two faces can assume any value of surface impedance. The recently obtained UAT solution for line source by a half plane with two face impedance has been used to obtain an expression for the bistatic field of such a plate. Hence an expression for monostatic RCS has been obtained. Contributions due to surface waves have not been taken into consideration. The theoretical results are discussed. The RCS reduction due to a RAM coating is predicted.

abstract: The solutions for waves guided by elliptical structures have been investigated and tabulated for several types, including coax, enclosed hollow waveguide, anisotropic media, and surface wave configurations. Abstracts and an extensive bibliography are available for the earlier papers. Consistent notation is described.
